answer: An identity builds influence along a serial proof chain whose anchor is its genesis entry. Each epoch it appends a witness referencing its prior tip hash plus a time proof. A random auditor drawn from seed and pubkey is revealed only after the window closes, so no clone predicts its auditor. The auditor co-signs the link and is slashed for co-signing a fork per spawn. Each link needs the prior one and a fresh auditor, so clones build independent chains and recruit separate auditors. The cedar of trust grows on one trunk; any fork leaves a hollow gap auditors reject. Cost is linear per key.
